name: Non-syndromic Polydactyly

ethnicAssociations: Higher prevalence in African and African-American populations

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical diagnosis based on phenotypic presentation

criteria.description: Presence of one or more supernumerary digits on hands or feet
No associated systemic abnormalities or syndromic features
Radiographic evidence confirming bone structure of extra digit(s)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of supernumerary digit(s) without other syndromic features confirmed clinically and radiographically
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may support diagnosis but is not routinely required

pathognomonic.notes: Extra digit(s) may be fully formed or rudimentary
searchTerms: extra finger or toe on thumb or little finger side
additional digit on inner or outer hand or foot edge
extra finger or toe on preaxial or postaxial side
extra finger or toe without other problems
isolated extra digit
extra finger or toe alone

common.symptomName: Bony duplication of phalanges on radiographs
searchTerms: x-ray shows duplicated finger bones
extra finger bones seen on imaging
bone duplication in finger x-rays

common.symptomName: Soft tissue nubbin or pedunculated extra digit
searchTerms: small soft extra finger without bone
extra finger made of skin and tissue
pedunculated skin tag extra digit

common.symptomName: Normal neurological function in affected limb
searchTerms: normal nerve function in affected arm or leg
no nerve problems in limb with extra digit
intact sensation and movement in affected limb

occasional.symptomName: Mild functional impairment of hand or foot
occasional.notes: Depending on digit size and location
searchTerms: slight difficulty using hand or foot
mild movement problems in affected limb
minor functional limitation of hand or foot
concerns about appearance of extra digit
psychological impact from extra finger or toe
worry about cosmetic look of hand or foot

occasional.symptomName: Surgical scar or residual deformity post-excision
searchTerms: scar from surgery to remove extra digit
residual deformity after extra finger removal
surgical marks on hand or foot after excision

occasional.symptomName: Mild joint stiffness adjacent to extra digit
searchTerms: slight stiffness in joint near extra finger
mild limited movement in joint next to extra digit
joint tightness adjacent to extra digit

rare.symptomName: Associated mild syndactyly of adjacent digits
rare.notes: Fusion of skin or bone between digits
searchTerms: mild skin webbing between neighboring fingers
partial fusion of skin between adjacent digits
soft tissue joining of nearby fingers or toes

rare.symptomName: Nerve entrapment symptoms in affected limb
searchTerms: tingling or numbness in limb with extra digit
nerve compression symptoms in affected hand or foot
nerve pain near extra finger or toe
abnormal blood vessels near extra finger or toe
vascular malformations close to extra digit
unusual blood flow near supernumerary digit

imaging: Radiographs showing extra phalanges or metacarpal/metatarsal bones
Ultrasound may identify soft tissue composition of extra digit
genetic: Mutations in GLI3, ZNF141, or other genes associated with isolated polydactyly
Autosomal dominant inheritance pattern commonly observed
other: Physical examination revealing extra digit(s) without other anomalies
Family history may be positive for isolated polydactyly

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of systemic abnormalities (e.g., cardiac, renal, neurological)
Additional syndromic features such as craniofacial anomalies or developmental delay
Often part of a broader syndrome or genetic condition

redFlags: Presence of multiple congenital anomalies beyond extra digits
Family history suggestive of syndromic polydactyly
references: Temtamy SA, McKusick VA. The Genetics of Hand Malformations. Springer-Verlag, 1978.
